issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may interfere with concurrent acquittals when the lower courts’ assessment overlooks vital evidence and causes a miscarriage of justice.
material_facts: The trial court and High Court rejected the complainants’ account in part because they considered it implausible that the complainants could possess the reported sum given their modest means.
The police recovered a substantial sum from the complainants’ home shortly after the complaint, supporting their account that they had returned with part of the money.
The lower courts failed to give proper weight to that recovery and to the absence of a reason for the complainants to make a false complaint against the accused, including police constables.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the lower courts’ approach resulted in an erroneous conclusion and a miscarriage of justice, and that the case warranted interference despite the concurrent findings of fact.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court ordinarily exercises self-restraint and does not reassess evidence, but may interfere on facts in a suitable case where the lower courts misread evidence or ignore vital evidence, resulting in a failure of justice. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an acquittal.
predicates.vital_evidence_overlooked: The lower courts failed to consider evidence material to assessing the prosecution account.
predicates.resulting_miscarriage_of_justice: The failure to consider that evidence led to an erroneous outcome and a miscarriage of justice.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquittal, vital evidence was overlooked, and that omission caused a miscarriage of justice, appellate interference is justified.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for robbery may be entered where the evidence proves the involvement of three accused in the taking, although the accused were charged with dacoity and the other accused are acquitted.
material_facts: The complainants testified that uniformed police constables stopped them, took them away from the bus, and removed money from the complainant’s person, with others present and participating.
The complaint recorded the number of one constable, and two other accused were already known to a complainant.
Money was recovered from three accused after statements they made led investigators to its locations; the Court considered the recoveries corroborative of the complainants’ evidence.
The Court found no dependable corroborative evidence against the other four accused and confirmed their acquittals.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the acquittals of the three accused whose involvement it found proved and convicted them of robbery rather than dacoity.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, because it confirmed the acquittal of four accused and convicted only three, conviction could properly be under Section 392 of the Indian Penal Code. It relied on the complainants’ evidence corroborated by the recoveries and other identification evidence; no earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_acquittal and taking_of_property_proved and accused_involvement_corroborated and fewer_than_five_accused_proved

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_acquittal: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging acquittals for a group taking of property.
predicates.taking_of_property_proved: The evidence establishes that property was taken from the complainants.
predicates.accused_involvement_corroborated: Evidence identifying the accused is supported by corroborative evidence, such as a recovery linked to their statements.
predicates.fewer_than_five_accused_proved: The evidence establishes the involvement of fewer than five accused in the taking.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal from acquittal, when the taking and corroborated involvement are proved but fewer than five accused are proved to have participated, the proper conviction is for robbery.

issues.legal_issue: A prosecution need not establish that recovered currency notes are individually identified as the exact notes taken from the complainants before a conviction may be based on the recovery.
material_facts: The complainants said that money was taken from them.
Investigators recovered money from three accused after statements made by those accused led to its discovery.
The accused argued that the recovered notes had to be shown to match the stolen notes.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the argument that the identities of the recovered currency notes had to match the stolen notes before a conviction could be recorded.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the recoveries, considered with the complainants’ evidence and the accused persons’ statements leading to discovery, as corroborative; it expressly rejected the proposed requirement of an exact match between the recovered notes and the notes taken. No provision or earlier case is cited for this point.

predicates.criminal_prosecution_for_taking_property: The proceeding is a criminal prosecution alleging that property was taken from a complainant.
predicates.recovered_money_linked_to_accused: Money was recovered from an accused in circumstances linking the recovery to that accused.
predicates.other_evidence_supports_taking: Evidence apart from the recovery supports the claim that property was taken from the complainant.

issues.definition: When a criminal prosecution is supported by evidence of a taking and recovered money is linked to an accused, an exact identification of the recovered notes is not required.

issues.legal_issue: An accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt when the evidence of identity is unreliable and there is no corroborative evidence of that accused’s involvement.
material_facts: The identification parades were held after the accused persons’ photographs had appeared in local newspapers and after they had been in police custody, so the possibility that witnesses had seen them beforehand could not be ruled out.
The Court found no corroborative evidence showing the involvement of four accused and considered the evidence regarding their identity unreliable.
The Court distinguished the three accused against whom it found corroborating evidence, including recoveries or prior identification.
issues.conclusion: The Court confirmed the acquittals of the four accused because their involvement lacked corroboration and the identification evidence was not dependable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court adopted a cautious approach to identification evidence and looked for corroboration in the circumstances of the case; where corroborative evidence was absent and identity evidence was unreliable, the accused were entitled to the benefit of doubt. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_case_identification_disputed: The proceeding is a criminal case in which the accused’s identity or identification by witnesses is disputed.
predicates.identification_evidence_unreliable: The circumstances make the witness identification evidence unreliable.
predicates.no_corroborative_evidence_of_involvement: There is no other evidence corroborating the accused’s involvement.

issues.definition: In a criminal case with disputed identity, unreliable identification and no corroboration of involvement entitle the accused to the benefit of doubt.

issues.legal_issue: The offence of unlawfully committing or keeping a person in confinement is not established by conduct amounting only to wrongful restraint.
material_facts: A police constable was charged with unlawfully committing or keeping the complainants in confinement.
The complainants were made to leave a bus and were taken to a nearby street.
The evidence did not show that they were kept in confinement at any time.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the charge was not proved because the conduct shown could amount at most to wrongful restraint, not wrongful confinement.
issues.legal_principle: For an offence under Section 220 of the Indian Penal Code, the accused must hold an office empowering the accused to commit a person for trial or confinement or to keep that person in confinement, and must corruptly or maliciously exercise that authority contrary to law with the required knowledge. The conduct must involve confinement; restraint alone is insufficient. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: criminal_charge_of_unlawful_confinement and authority_to_commit_or_confine and corrupt_or_malicious_unlawful_exercise and not person_kept_in_confinement

predicates.criminal_charge_of_unlawful_confinement: The proceeding includes a criminal charge alleging an unlawful exercise of authority to commit or keep a person in confinement.
predicates.authority_to_commit_or_confine: The accused held an office empowering the accused to commit a person for trial or confinement or to keep a person in confinement.
predicates.corrupt_or_malicious_unlawful_exercise: The accused corruptly or maliciously exercised that authority contrary to law, knowing the exercise was unlawful.
predicates.person_kept_in_confinement: The accused actually kept the person in confinement.

issues.definition: Even where the accused had authority and exercised it corruptly or maliciously contrary to law, the confinement charge is not proved if the person was not kept in confinement.

issues.legal_issue: An accused convicted for the first time on appeal must be given an opportunity to be heard on sentence before sentence is imposed.
material_facts: The Supreme Court convicted three accused for the first time in that Court.
The Court deferred the matter and directed that the accused be heard on the question of sentence.
issues.conclusion: The Court ordered that the newly convicted accused be given an opportunity to be heard on sentence before sentence was imposed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires an opportunity to be heard on the question of sentence after conviction. The Court applied that requirement because it was convicting the accused for the first time; no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The proceeding is a criminal appeal.
predicates.accused_convicted_for_first_time_on_appe: The accused is convicted for the first time by the appellate court.
predicates.sentence_not_yet_imposed: The appellate court has not yet imposed sentence on the newly convicted accused.

issues.definition: When an accused is convicted for the first time in a criminal appeal and sentence has not yet been imposed, the accused must be heard on sentence.
